title: Foundation to DPC
headline: Everything below the floor: trenches, footings, foundation walls and the ground slab up to damp-proof level.
seoTitle: Foundation to DPC in Nigeria: trenches, footings, blockwork and German floor explained
seoDescription: Plain-English guide to strip and pad foundations, blinding, foundation blockwork, filling, DPM and the ground floor slab, with tricks to watch for and photos to request.
summary: This is the stage you cannot easily inspect later. Insist on photos and measurements before anything is covered.
duration: 2–5 weeks for a bungalow; longer for storey buildings or difficult soil [CHECK]
whatHappens: Excavation of trenches (for strip foundations) or pits (for column bases) to the depth and width on the structural drawing — often around 0.9 m deep for bungalows on firm soil. [CHECK against your drawings]
Blinding: a thin layer of weak concrete (about 50 mm) at the bottom of the trench to give a clean, level base.
Footing: reinforced or mass concrete strip, or reinforced column bases, cast to the drawing (e.g. 675 × 225 mm strip for a 9-inch wall — your engineer decides). [CHECK]
Foundation blockwork: usually 9-inch blocks filled solid with concrete from footing to just above ground (DPC level). Column starters are cast here for framed buildings.
Backfilling and compacting the inside with laterite in layers, then hardcore (broken stone).
Anti-termite treatment of the ground, then a damp-proof membrane (polythene, DPM) and the ground floor slab (often called ‘German floor’), commonly 100–150 mm thick, sometimes with BRC mesh.
problems: Trenches dug shallower or narrower than the drawing.
No blinding, or blinding done after rain with mud in the trench.
Weak concrete: too little cement, too much water, or dirty sand. Ask how many bags per mix.
Rods smaller than specified (Y10 instead of Y12) or fewer of them; or the right rods bought but resold.
Foundation blocks not filled solid, or hollow 6-inch blocks used instead of 9-inch.
Laterite dumped in one go without compaction — the floor settles and cracks later.
DPM skipped or torn, causing damp and peeling paint inside.
Slab poured thinner than agreed, or not cured with water for at least 7 days.
questions: What depth and width are the trenches, and do they match the structural drawing?
What concrete mix are you using for blinding, footing and slab, and how many bags per mix?
What rod sizes and spacing are in the footings and column bases?
Are the foundation blocks 9-inch and filled solid with concrete?
How is the fill compacted, and in what layer thickness?
Has anti-termite treatment and DPM been done before the slab?
How long will the slab be cured (kept wet)?
photoCheckpoints: Trench with a tape measure showing depth and width at several points, before blinding.

Concrete being mixed, showing cement bags counted per mix.
